meta.title: Appendix A: Survey
meta.note: Source values marked with ~ (about 6.25% and about 0%) are stored as 6.25 and 0.

questions.text: Before hearing about this case, were you familiar with d4vd's music?

options.label: Yes, I listened often
Yes, I knew some songs
I knew of him but did not listen
No

questions.text: Do you think it is possible to separate an artist's work from the artist's personal actions?

options.label: Yes
Sometimes
No

questions.text: If an artist is accused of a serious violent crime but has not been convicted, should listeners stop supporting their music?

options.label: Yes, immediately
Yes, but only temporarily until more facts are known
No, people should wait for a court decision
No, never

questions.text: If an artist is convicted of murder, would you continue to listen to their music?

options.label: Stop supporting the artist immediately
Wait for more evidence before deciding
Wait for the result of the trial
Continue listening because allegations are not proof
It depends on the seriousness of the allegation

questions.text: Do you think an artist's alleged or proven actions can change the meaning of their songs?

options.label: Yes, completely
Yes, somewhat
No, the music stays separate from the artist
It depends on the song and the situation

questions.text: Which factor would most affect your decision to keep supporting an artist accused of serious wrongdoing?

options.label: The seriousness of the allegation
Whether there is strong evidence
Whether the artist is convicted in court
My personal connection to the artist's music
Whether the artist profits from my support

questions.text: Do you think fans have a responsibility to consider the ethical behavior of artists they support?

options.label: Yes, definitely
Yes, but only in very serious cases
No, art and personal behavior should stay separate
No, fans are not responsible for an artist's actions

field_notes: {s:1:2} of respondents knew some of the artist's songs before the case.
Only {s:6:3} said a court verdict would be the deciding factor.
{s:3:2} would pause support temporarily until more facts are known.
